answer: Restricting a function's domain can make it possible to define an inverse because it allows the function to become one-to-one. A function that is not one-to-one cannot have an inverse, as there would be multiple outputs for a single input. By selecting a subset of the original domain where the function behaves in a one-to-one manner, we can define a new function with this restricted domain. This new function can then have an inverse defined on that domain. For example, if a function is one-to-one on a specific interval, we can restrict its domain to that interval, allowing us to define an inverse function for it [openstax_calculus_v1_p0079_s0_paragraph_0000].

The domain of a trigonometric function must be restricted to define an inverse because the basic trigonometric functions are periodic and therefore not one-to-one over their entire domains. By restricting the domain to an interval where the function is one-to-one, we can define its inverse. For example, the sine function can be made one-to-one by restricting its domain to a specific interval, allowing us to define the inverse sine function on that restricted domain [openstax_calculus_v1_p0080_s0_paragraph_0001].

An exponential function is distinguished from a power function by having a constant base and a variable exponent. In contrast, a power function has a variable base and a constant exponent. Specifically, an exponential function can be expressed in the form \( a^x \) where \( a \) is a constant, while a power function is of the form \( x^n \) where \( n \) is a constant [openstax_calculus_v1_p0088_s0_paragraph_0003].
